title: Context propagation: traceparent and baggage
summary: How one trace survives crossing processes: the W3C traceparent and tracestate headers, baggage, and what .NET injects for you.

steps.title: The traceparent header
body: A trace crosses services because each outgoing call carries the current span's context in a header, defined by the W3C
**Trace Context** recommendation:
```text
traceparent: 00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01
version  trace-id (16 bytes, 32 hex)    parent-id         flags (01 = sampled)
(8 bytes, 16 hex)
- Lowercase hex only. A trace id or parent id of all zeros is invalid. Version `ff` is invalid; version `00` has exactly four parts.
- The receiver starts its server span as a **child** of `parent-id`, in the same trace, and follows the **sampled** flag
(parent-based sampling, lesson 4).
- **`tracestate`** carries vendor-specific values alongside it (`tracestate: ot=th:8,vendor=abc`), up to 32 entries.
In .NET you rarely write this: `HttpClient` injects `traceparent` from `Activity.Current` on every request, and ASP.NET Core extracts
it on every incoming one (both through `DistributedContextPropagator.Current`, W3C by default). You do it by hand where no library
does: message headers, a custom TCP protocol, a job queue in a database table.

steps.explain: The second part is the trace id (the first 8 hex digits are printed), the third the parent span id (16 hex digits), and the lowest bit of the flags is `sampled`. Only that bit is defined today (bit 2, `random`, is in Trace Context Level 2); test the bit, never compare the whole byte to `01`.

steps.title: Parse traceparent like a receiver must
prompt: Write `bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)` for version `00` headers.
- the header has exactly four `-`-separated parts: version `00`, trace id, parent id, flags;
- the trace id is 32 and the parent id 16 **lowercase** hex digits, and neither is all zeros;
`sampled` is bit 0 of the flags. Leading or trailing spaces around the whole header are allowed (trim them).
A receiver that rejects a bad header simply starts a new trace, so be strict.
starter: bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)
solution: bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)
static bool Hex(string s, int len) => s.Length == len && s.All(c => c is >= '0' and <= '9' or >= 'a' and <= 'f');
if (parts[1].All(c => c == '0') || parts[2].All(c => c == '0')) return false;
hints: A small helper `bool Hex(string s, int len)` that checks the length and that every char is `0-9` or `a-f` covers three checks.
Set the `out` values only after every check passed, so a rejected header leaves them empty.
template: {{CODE}}

Dojo.Check("a valid sampled header", TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", out var t1, out var p1, out var s1) && t1 == "46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f" && p1 == "86d88d2ffaed6bdf" && s1, "");
Dojo.Check("not sampled (00)", TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-00", out _, out _, out var s2) && !s2, "");
Dojo.Check("flags 09: bit 0 set, so sampled", TryParse(" 00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-09 ", out _, out _, out var s3) && s3, "");
Dojo.Check("uppercase hex is rejected", !TryParse("00-46AE7E540484DD36A9DF49AAB2401A3F-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("all-zero trace id is rejected", !TryParse("00-00000000000000000000000000000000-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("all-zero parent id is rejected", !TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-0000000000000000-01", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("short trace id is rejected", !TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("version ff is rejected", !TryParse("ff-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("a fifth part is rejected for version 00", !TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01-xyz", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("null and empty are rejected", !TryParse(null, out var t9, out _, out _) && t9 == "" && !TryParse("", out _, out _, out _), "");
Dojo.Check("non-hex flags are rejected", !TryParse("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-0g", out _, out _, out _), "");

steps.title: Propagate to the next hop
prompt: When your service calls the next one, the header carries **your** span as the parent. Write
`string Outgoing(string incoming, string mySpanId)`: the header to send downstream, with the incoming trace id, `mySpanId` as the
parent id, and the incoming flags unchanged. If `incoming` is not a valid header (reuse `TryParse`, paste it in), start a new
trace: return `"00-" + NewTraceId() + "-" + mySpanId + "-01"` (the tests give you `string NewTraceId()`).
solution: if (!TryParse(incoming, out var traceId, out _, out _)) return "00-" + NewTraceId() + "-" + mySpanId + "-01";
bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)
static bool Hex(string s, int len) => s.Length == len && s.All(c => c is >= '0' and <= '9' or >= 'a' and <= 'f');
if (parts[1].All(c => c == '0') || parts[2].All(c => c == '0')) return false;
hints: Keep the flags exactly as they came (`00` must stay `00`: the caller decided not to sample, and you follow).
template: string NewTraceId() => "aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111";
{{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("same trace, my span as the parent", "00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-9e324d19633e0502-01", Outgoing("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-01", "9e324d19633e0502"));
Dojo.Eq("an unsampled trace stays unsampled", "00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-9e324d19633e0502-00", Outgoing("00-46ae7e540484dd36a9df49aab2401a3f-86d88d2ffaed6bdf-00", "9e324d19633e0502"));
Dojo.Eq("garbage in: a new trace", "00-aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-9e324d19633e0502-01", Outgoing("not-a-header", "9e324d19633e0502"));
Dojo.Eq("no header: a new trace", "00-aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1111222233334444-01", Outgoing("", "1111222233334444"));

steps.title: Baggage: context that is not about timing
body: **Baggage** is a second header (`baggage: tenant.id=acme,user.tier=gold;ttl=60`) that carries key/value pairs to every downstream
service, so a service deep in the call chain can know the tenant or the experiment group without every API passing it along.
- It is **not** added to spans automatically: a service reads it and copies what it needs onto its spans or metrics (in the .NET
SDK, `Baggage.GetBaggage("tenant.id")`; a `BaggageSpanProcessor` can copy all of it).
- It travels in plain text to every service you call, *including third parties*. Never put secrets, tokens or personal data in it.
- Keep it small: it is sent on every request (the W3C spec limits it to 8 192 bytes and 64 entries).
- Values are percent-encoded; anything after `;` is a property of that entry.
`OTEL_PROPAGATORS` picks the formats an SDK reads and writes (default `tracecontext,baggage`; `b3` and `jaeger` exist for old
systems you still talk to).

steps.prompt: Which of these belongs in baggage?
options: `tenant.id=acme`, so every service can tag its spans and metrics with the tenant
`auth=Bearer eyJhbGciOi...`, so downstream services can call on the user's behalf
`user.email=ana@example.com`, so support can search traces by customer
the whole cart as JSON, so inventory does not need to load it
steps.explain: Baggage is propagated to every hop, in plain text, possibly outside your company: small, non-sensitive, useful for correlation. Credentials belong in their own headers with their own rules, personal data nowhere it can leak, and payloads in the request body.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: propagation
steps.body: The APIs and settings that decide whether a trace survives the next hop.

toolkit.what: The span running on this async flow right now: what HttpClient and loggers attach to.
flags: the trace id to put in an error response or a log
an ActivityContext to pass on or to link
toolkit.example: return Results.Problem(detail: "Payment failed", extensions: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["traceId"] = Activity.Current?.TraceId.ToString() });
toolkit.when: showing users a trace id they can quote to support

toolkit.what: Write the current context (traceparent, tracestate, baggage) into any carrier: message headers, a dictionary.
flags: consumer side: returns the parent context
toolkit.example: Propagators.DefaultTextMapPropagator.Inject(new PropagationContext(activity!.Context, Baggage.Current), message.Headers, (h, k, v) => h[k] = v);
toolkit.when: queues, jobs, anything that is not HTTP or gRPC

toolkit.what: Which propagation formats the SDK reads and writes.
flags: Zipkin's B3 headers, for older systems
toolkit.when: talking to a system that only knows B3

toolkit.what: Join a request to a trace you choose, then find it by that id in the backend.
toolkit.when: reproducing a bug and wanting its trace without searching

steps.title: Read the baggage header
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string> ParseBaggage(string? header)` for the W3C `baggage` header:
- entries are separated by `,`; each is `key=value`, optionally followed by `;properties` (ignore properties);
- trim spaces around keys and values; skip entries without `=` or with an empty key;
- values are percent-encoded: decode them with `Uri.UnescapeDataString`;
- if a key repeats, the **last** one wins.
hints: Split on `,`, then keep only what comes before the first `;`, then split at the first `=` (values may contain `=` after encoding... take everything after the first one).
`result[key] = value` (the indexer) makes the last duplicate win.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoB = ParseBaggage("tenant.id=acme, user.tier=gold;ttl=60,note=caf%C3%A9");
Dojo.Eq("three entries", 3, dojoB.Count);
Dojo.Eq("tenant.id", "acme", dojoB.GetValueOrDefault("tenant.id"));
Dojo.Eq("properties after ; are not part of the value", "gold", dojoB.GetValueOrDefault("user.tier"));
Dojo.Eq("percent-decoded", "café", dojoB.GetValueOrDefault("note"));
Dojo.Eq("last one wins", "b", ParseBaggage("k=a,k=b").GetValueOrDefault("k"));
Dojo.Eq("junk entries skipped", 1, ParseBaggage("novalue,=x, ok = yes ,").Count);
Dojo.Eq("spaces trimmed", "yes", ParseBaggage("novalue,=x, ok = yes ,").GetValueOrDefault("ok"));
Dojo.Eq("null header", 0, ParseBaggage(null).Count);
